title: String::parse_url misparses query-only URLs without explicit slash.  Impacts HTTPRequest and WebSocketPeer
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced in v4.6.2.stable.mono.official.71f334935

Present by source inspection on master at [fa6cad230f638d65a5a897008c5fc512edc237ad](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fa6cad230f638d65a5a897008c5fc512edc237ad/core/string/ustring.cpp)
Present by source inspection on 4.5 at [529a652bd5766b6ba4da2ac0f0f9322e8f8daa1d](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/529a652bd5766b6ba4da2ac0f0f9322e8f8daa1d/core/string/ustring.cpp)

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9579) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 63.74 GiB memory

### Issue description

A URL such as https://httpbin.org?token=abc is valid and should be equivalent, for HTTP request-target purposes, to https://httpbin.org/?token=abc.

In Godot 4.6.2, HTTPRequest fails for the slashless query form but succeeds when an explicit / is added before the query.  Easy enough to work around, but a bit painful and mysterious to root-cause when it fails.

The root cause appears to be in String::parse_url(), where path is split on the first '/' character, but not '?'.  Particulary,  code around line 250, below does not consider '?' as a possible terminator.  Probably should split at first '?' or '/'.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4c311cbee68c0b66ff8ebb8b0defdd9979dd2a41/core/string/ustring.cpp#L220-L300

### Steps to reproduce

Code below will repro the issue.  Inspect output in debug window.  Expected behavior is both calls to test to succeed.  Only second one does.  
```
extends Node


func _ready() -> void:
	test("https://httpbin.org?token=abc")    # this fails, but should work like the second call
	await get_tree().create_timer(3.0).timeout
	test("https://httpbin.org/?token=abc")   # this succeeds

func test(url: String) -> void:
	var req := HTTPRequest.new()
	add_child(req)
	req.request_completed.connect(func(result, response_code, headers, body):
		print("--- ", url)
		print("result=", result, " response_code=", response_code)
		print(body.get_string_from_utf8())
		req.queue_free()
	)
	var err := req.request(url)
	print("request err=", err, " url=", url)
```
